- When sentiment is positive (≥0.33) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.33), model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if price is falling.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp upward spikes in sentiment; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent peak if sentiment remains bullish.
- If sentiment is mixed or neutral, model shows persistent lag; forecast should align with recent 5–7 day moving average.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >10% above recent 18-day high, reduce by 5–10% unless sentiment strongly supports.
- If sentiment turns negative after a spike, model often fails to correct; add a downward bias of 2–5% for 3–5 days post-spike.
- Forecast should not exceed 15% above 30-day moving average unless sentiment is strongly bullish and sustained.
